items.snippet_en: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that COVID-19 vaccines do not contain microchips and are not administered to track movement. Their purpose is to stimulate the immune system to produce antibodies against the disease.

The Mayo Clinic explicitly states that there are no microchips in the vaccine and no way for it to track people or gather personal information. The origin of this myth has been linked to misinterpretations of comments made by Bill Gates about digital vaccine records.

The claim that COVID-19 vaccines contain microchips for tracking vaccinated individuals is false. This conspiracy theory has been widely debunked by health organizations, government bodies, and fact-checkers.

Pfizer confirms that its vaccines do not contain microchips or any other tracking devices. The claim that COVID-19 vaccines contain microchips for tracking vaccinated individuals is false.

The Indonesian Ministry of Communication and Information (Kominfo) has declared information about microchips in COVID-19 vaccines as a hoax. They clarify that barcodes on vaccine products are for tracking distribution, not individuals.

The Indonesian National Police confirmed that claims of Pfizer receiving a patent to track vaccinated individuals are false, and Pfizer itself has denied such patents.
Experts explain that the physical size of microchips makes it impossible for them to be injected through a standard vaccine needle.
